question: Which of the following titles means "Lord of the three worlds"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tribhuvana-chakravartin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The title Tribhuvana-chakravartin (त्रिभुवन-चक्रवर्तिन्) literally means the 'Lord/Universal ruler of the three worlds', combining 'Tribhuvana' (three worlds — heaven, earth and the netherworld) with 'Chakravartin' (a universal, world-conquering monarch).

• It was an exalted imperial title adopted by powerful South Indian dynasties, most notably the Cholas, to project their sovereignty and paramountcy.

• Such grand titles were used in inscriptions to glorify the king and assert supremacy over other rulers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• 'Chakravartin' is an ancient Indian concept of an ideal universal ruler whose chariot wheels roll unobstructed in all directions.

• Cholas like Rajaraja I and Rajendra I assumed a string of high-sounding titles reflecting their conquests.

NOTE

• Maharaja-adhiraja (Option 1): A title meaning 'great king of kings', used by many North Indian rulers such as the Guptas.

• Ekrat-Samrat (Option 3): Titles ('Ekarat', 'Samrat') associated with a sole/supreme sovereign in Vedic tradition, not the 'three worlds'.

• Devaraja (Option 4): Means 'god-king'; a concept of divine kingship famously associated with Southeast Asian (Khmer) polity.

question: By which of the following amendment act of the Indian constitution voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 61st Amendment act, 1989.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1989 (61वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम) reduced the voting age for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from 21 years to 18 years.

• It amended Article 326 of the Constitution, which deals with elections on the basis of adult suffrage.

• It was enacted during the tenure of PM Rajiv Gandhi to give the youth a greater voice in the democratic process.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The amendment came into force in 1989, enabling younger citizens to vote from the 1989 general elections onwards.

• Adult suffrage means every citizen above the prescribed age can vote without discrimination.

NOTE

• 62nd Amendment act, 1989 (Option 2): Extended the reservation of seats for SCs/STs and Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for a further period.

• 63rd Amendment act, 1989 (Option 3): Related to Punjab and repealed provisions concerning emergency in that state (amending Art. 356).

• 64th Amendment act, 1990 (Option 4): Extended President's Rule in Punjab beyond the normal period.

question: G.S.T. was implemented through which constitutional amendment act of constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 101st Amendment act, 2016.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 (101वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम).

• GST was rolled out on 1 July 2017 as a unified indirect tax subsuming multiple central and state levies (excise, service tax, VAT, etc.).

• The amendment inserted Article 279A providing for the constitution of the GST Council.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• GST is a destination-based, multi-stage tax levied on every value addition.

• The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister with state finance ministers as members.

NOTE

• 100th Amendment act, 2015 (Option 1): Gave effect to the Land Boundary Agreement between India and Bangladesh (exchange of enclaves).

• 102nd Amendment act, 2018 (Option 3): Granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).

• 103rd Amendment act, 2019 (Option 4): Provided 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).

question: In March 2025, Minister of State Shri Pabitra Margherita received Honorary Order of Freedom of Barbados Award on behalf of _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In March 2025, Minister of State for External Affairs Pabitra Margherita received the 'Honorary Order of Freedom of Barbados' on behalf of Prime Minister Narendra Modi (प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी).

• The award was conferred on PM Modi for his leadership and India's humanitarian assistance, especially supply of COVID-19 vaccines to Barbados.

• It is the highest national honour of Barbados.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• PM Modi dedicated the honour to the 1.4 billion people of India.

• Barbados is a Caribbean island nation that became a republic in 2021.

NOTE

• External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar (Option 1): India's Minister of External Affairs; the award was not on his behalf.

• Defence Minister Rajnath Singh (Option 3): India's Defence Minister; unrelated to this award.

• Home Affairs Minister Amit Shah (Option 4): India's Union Home Minister; unrelated to this award.

question:
Integration of TB services within the public health system is essential for India to achieve which of the following goals?
I. Eradication of malaria
II. Equitable and universal health coverage
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Integrating Tuberculosis (TB) services within the general public health system is essential for achieving equitable and universal health coverage (समान और सार्वभौमिक स्वास्थ्य कवरेज).

• TB is a disease of the lungs caused by the bacterium *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*, whereas malaria is a mosquito-borne parasitic disease — so statement I (eradication of malaria) is unrelated.

• Universal Health Coverage (UHC) ensures all people have access to needed health services without financial hardship.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India runs the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP) aiming to end TB.

• UHC is part of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3 — Good Health and Well-being.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, as malaria eradication is not linked to integrating TB services.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since statement I is not a relevant goal here.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because statement II is a valid goal.

question: Which scheme was launched by the Union Government in December 2024 to incentivize cargo movement via inland waterways?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jalvahak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Jalvahak' scheme (जलवाहक) was launched by the Union Government in December 2024 to incentivize long-haul cargo movement through inland waterways.

• It was launched by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways and offers incentives for cargo transported over 300 km.

• It targets the national waterways NW-1 (Ganga), NW-2 (Brahmaputra) and NW-16 (Barak).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme aims to reduce logistics costs and congestion on road and rail networks.

• The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) implements inland water transport development.

NOTE

• Jalshakti (Option 1): Refers to the Ministry of Jal Shakti (water resources); not this cargo scheme.

• Ganga Freight Initiative (Option 3): Not an official Government scheme name in this context.

• Sagarmala (Option 4): A programme for port-led development and coastal shipping, launched in 2015.

question: Which index is the world's first Government-led sub-national measure of SDG progress?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SDG India Index.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The SDG India Index (एस.डी.जी. भारत सूचकांक) is the world's first Government-led sub-national measure of progress on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

• It is developed and released by NITI Aayog to rank States and Union Territories on their SDG performance.

• It was first launched in 2018 and is updated periodically.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The 17 SDGs were adopted by the United Nations in 2015 to be achieved by 2030.

• States are scored and classified as Aspirant, Performer, Front-Runner or Achiever.

NOTE

• China Leading SDG Index (Option 2): Not an established Government-led global SDG measure of this kind.

• American Sustainable Index (Option 3): Not a recognised official SDG measurement index.

• SDG EU Index (Option 4): Not the world's first sub-national Government-led SDG index.

question: Who won gold in the 10m Air Pistol event (Women) at the Asian Games 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Palak Gulia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Palak Gulia (पलक गुलिया) won the gold medal in the 10m Air Pistol (Women) individual event at the Asian Games 2023 held in Hangzhou, China.

• Her compatriot Esha Singh won the silver in the same event, making it a 1-2 finish for India.

• The Asian Games 2023 were held in 2023 (postponed edition) and India had a record medal haul.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Shooting was one of India's strongest sports at the 2023 Asian Games.

• Palak Gulia is a young Indian pistol shooter from Haryana.

NOTE

• Esha Singh (Option 2): Won silver in the individual 10m Air Pistol (Women) event, not gold.

• Ramita (Option 3): Ramita Jindal is an Indian shooter associated with the 10m Air Rifle event.

• Rutuja Bhosale (Option 4): An Indian tennis player, not a shooter.

question: What was India's position on the medal table at Paris Olympics 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 71.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India finished at the 71st position (71वां स्थान) on the medal table at the Paris Olympics 2024.

• India won a total of 6 medals — 1 silver and 5 bronze — with no gold, which pushed its rank lower on the standings.

• The medal table is ranked primarily by number of gold medals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Neeraj Chopra won the silver in men's javelin throw; Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals in shooting.

• The United States topped the Paris 2024 medal tally.

NOTE

• 28 (Option 1): Not India's rank at Paris 2024.

• 23 (Option 2): Not India's rank at Paris 2024.

• 91 (Option 3): Not India's rank at Paris 2024.

question: In track events, key rules are related to how many phases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In track events, the key rules are broadly related to three (3) phases (तीन चरण) — the start, the run (running phase) and the finish.

• Each phase has specific rules, such as the starting procedure (blocks/false start), lane discipline during the run, and finishing at the line.

• Proper technique in each phase determines fair competition and results.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Track events are running/racing competitions held on the athletics track, distinct from field events.

• A false start in the start phase can lead to disqualification.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 1): Understates the phases; the standard division is three.

• 4 (Option 3): Not the standard number of key rule phases in track events.

• 5 (Option 4): Not the standard number of key rule phases in track events.

question: What is the primary objective of device "AroTrack", which was launched by IIT Bombay in December 2024?
option_3: To detect the moisture level in environment.
option_4: To monitor the air quality level.
solution_text:
The correct answer is To detect water pollutants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The device 'AroTrack', developed by IIT Bombay (December 2024), is primarily designed to detect water pollutants (जल प्रदूषकों का पता लगाना).

• It is a portable, biosensor-based device that can rapidly detect toxic contaminants such as phenol and related pollutants in water.

• It provides real-time, on-site water quality monitoring even in remote areas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Such biosensors help ensure safe drinking water and monitor industrial effluents.

• IIT Bombay is a premier engineering and research institute in India.

NOTE

• To surveillance the railway track (Option 2): Not the function of AroTrack.

• To detect the moisture level in environment (Option 3): Not the purpose of this device.

• To monitor the air quality level (Option 4): AroTrack is for water, not air, quality.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The Room on the Roof'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ruskin Bond.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'The Room on the Roof' was written by the celebrated Indian author Ruskin Bond (रस्किन बॉन्ड).

• It was his debut novel, written when he was just 17, and it won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957.

• The novel is semi-autobiographical, centred on a young Anglo-Indian boy named Rusty in Dehradun.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ruskin Bond is known for works like 'The Blue Umbrella', 'A Flight of Pigeons' and 'Rusty' series.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (1999) and Padma Bhushan (2014).

NOTE

• Shashi Tharoor (Option 1): Author of works like 'The Great Indian Novel' and 'An Era of Darkness'.

• R. K. Narayan (Option 2): Author of 'Malgudi Days' and 'Swami and Friends'.

• V.S. Naipaul (Option 3): Nobel laureate, author of 'A House for Mr Biswas' and 'A Bend in the River'.

question: Which of the following temples is also known as "Black Pagoda"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sun Temple, Konark.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sun Temple at Konark, Odisha (सूर्य मंदिर, कोणार्क) is also known as the 'Black Pagoda'.

• It was built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.

• The temple is designed in the shape of a colossal chariot of the Sun God Surya, with 24 carved wheels and seven horses.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 1984).

• European sailors called it the 'Black Pagoda' as a navigational landmark, in contrast to the 'White Pagoda' (Jagannath Temple, Puri).

NOTE

• Meenakshi Temple, Madurai (Option 2): A famous Dravidian temple in Tamil Nadu dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi.

• Sri Venkateswara Temple, Tirupati (Option 3): A major Vaishnavite temple in Andhra Pradesh dedicated to Lord Venkateswara.

• Lingaraj Temple, Bhubaneswar (Option 4): A large Kalinga-style temple in Odisha dedicated to Lord Shiva (Harihara).

question: 'Chhappar Mela' is held in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Chhappar Mela' (छप्पर मेला) is a famous traditional fair held in the state of Punjab.

• It is held at the village of Chhappar in Ludhiana district in honour of the deity Gugga (Gugga Peer/Snake God).

• The fair typically takes place in the month of Bhadon (August–September).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is one of the largest fairs of the Malwa region of Punjab.

• Punjab is known for fairs and festivals like Baisakhi, Lohri and Hola Mohalla.

NOTE

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Known for tribal festivals like Sarhul and Karma, not the Chhappar Mela.

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Known for festivals like Pongal and temple fairs, not this mela.

• Goa (Option 4): Known for the Carnival and Shigmo festival, not the Chhappar Mela.

question: Which emperor's reign saw great advancements in Mauryan architecture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashoka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reign of Emperor Ashoka (अशोक) saw great advancements in Mauryan architecture.

• Ashoka is famous for the polished sandstone pillars (Ashokan pillars), rock-cut caves (Barabar caves) and stupas such as the Sanchi Stupa.

• The Lion Capital of Sarnath, built under Ashoka, is now India's National Emblem.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War and spread the Dhamma.

• His edicts were inscribed on pillars and rocks across the empire.

NOTE

• Bimbisara (Option 1): A ruler of the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha, a contemporary of the Buddha (pre-Mauryan).

• Bindusara (Option 2): Ashoka's father and the second Mauryan emperor.

• Ajatashatru (Option 4): A Haryanka dynasty king of Magadha, son of Bimbisara (pre-Mauryan).

question: 'Kandali' festival is celebrated in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Kandali' festival (कंडाली) is celebrated in the state of Uttarakhand, in the Chaundas Valley of the Pithoragarh district.

• It is celebrated by the Rung (Shauka) tribal community and takes place once in about 12 years, when the Kandali flower (a kind of buckwheat) blooms.

• The festival has legends linking it to the community's victory over invaders.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Uttarakhand is also known for festivals like Harela, Phool Dei and the Nanda Devi Raj Jat.

• The Rung community lives in the higher Himalayan regions of Kumaon.

NOTE

• Goa (Option 1): Known for the Carnival and Shigmo festival, not Kandali.

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Known for Ganesh Chaturthi and Gudi Padwa, not Kandali.

• West Bengal (Option 3): Known for Durga Puja and Poila Boishakh, not Kandali.

question: Which traditional dance of Mizoram is performed to celebrate victory in war?
solution_text:
The correct answer is So Lakia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• So Lakia (Solakia/Sarlamkai) (सोलकिया) is a traditional dance of Mizoram performed to celebrate victory in war.

• It is a war-victory dance of the Pawi and Mara (Lakher) tribes, traditionally performed after triumph over enemies.

• Dancers, often dressed as warriors, move to the beat of gongs and drums.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Cheraw (the bamboo dance) is the most famous folk dance of Mizoram.

• Mizoram's dances are usually performed during festivals like Chapchar Kut.

NOTE

• Kodava (Option 1): Refers to the Kodava (Coorg) community of Karnataka; not a Mizoram war dance.

• Chamba (Option 2): Associated with Himachal Pradesh (Chamba region), not Mizoram.

• Dumhal (Option 4): A traditional dance of the Wattal tribe of Jammu and Kashmir.

question: In which year did Tipu Sultan become the ruler of Mysore?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1782.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tipu Sultan (टीपू सुल्तान) became the ruler of Mysore in 1782, after the death of his father Hyder Ali.

• Known as the 'Tiger of Mysore', he continued the wars against the British East India Company.

• He introduced administrative and military reforms and is credited with early use of iron-cased rockets (Mysorean rockets).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tipu Sultan died in 1799 defending Srirangapatna in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

• He fought the Second, Third and Fourth Anglo-Mysore Wars against the British.

NOTE

• 1788 (Option 2): Not the year he ascended the throne; he was already ruling by then.

• 1795 (Option 3): Falls between the Third and Fourth Anglo-Mysore Wars, not his accession year.

• 1799 (Option 4): The year of Tipu Sultan's death, not his accession.

question: A committee was set up in _____ under the chairmanship of R.N. Malhotra, former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, to make recommendations for reforms in the insurance sector.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1993.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Malhotra Committee was set up in 1993 (1993) under the chairmanship of R.N. Malhotra, a former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, to recommend reforms in the insurance sector.

• The committee submitted its report in 1994, recommending opening up the insurance sector to private players.

• Its recommendations led to the establishment of the IRDA (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority) in 1999–2000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The committee suggested reducing the state monopoly of LIC and GIC and allowing private and foreign participation.

• IRDAI is the regulator of the insurance industry in India, headquartered in Hyderabad.

NOTE

• 1992 (Option 1): Not the year the Malhotra Committee was constituted.

• 1995 (Option 3): Not the year of the committee's formation.

• 1996 (Option 4): Not the year of the committee's formation.

question: What is the first hour of Lok Sabha proceedings called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Question hour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first hour of the sitting of the Lok Sabha (and Rajya Sabha) is called the Question Hour (प्रश्नकाल).

• During this hour, members ask questions and ministers are required to answer, ensuring executive accountability.

• Questions are of three kinds — Starred (oral answer), Unstarred (written answer) and Short Notice questions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Question Hour is generally the first hour of a parliamentary sitting.

• It is mentioned in the Rules of Procedure of the House, not directly in the Constitution.

NOTE

• Public hour (Option 1): Not a recognised term for parliamentary proceedings.

• Privilege hour (Option 2): Not a standard parliamentary term; parliamentary privileges are a separate concept.

• Zero hour (Option 4): The informal period immediately following the Question Hour, when members raise urgent matters without prior notice.

question: Which of the following is an example of temperate and subtropical crop?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wheat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Wheat (गेहूँ) is an example of a temperate and subtropical crop.

• It is a rabi (winter) crop, sown in winter and harvested in spring, requiring cool growing conditions and moderate rainfall.

• Wheat is the second most important cereal (staple food) crop of India after rice.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Major wheat-producing states include Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Madhya Pradesh and Haryana.

• Wheat needs bright sunshine at the time of ripening.

NOTE

• Jute (Option 2): A tropical fibre crop that grows in hot, humid climates with high rainfall (e.g., West Bengal).

• Cotton (Option 3): A tropical/subtropical kharif fibre crop needing high temperatures and black soil.

• Cucumber (Option 4): A warm-season vegetable crop, generally grown in summer, not classed as a temperate cereal crop.

question: According to the Census 2011, which state had a negative growth rate in decadal population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census 2011, Nagaland (नगालैंड) was the only state to record a negative decadal population growth rate (about −0.58%) during 2001–2011.

• This means Nagaland's population actually declined compared to the 2001 Census figure.

• Nagaland is a hilly north-eastern state that attained statehood in 1963.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census and the 7th after independence.

• The most populous state in Census 2011 was Uttar Pradesh.

NOTE

• Mizoram (Option 2): A north-eastern state; it did not record a negative decadal growth rate in Census 2011.

• Daman & Diu (Option 3): A Union Territory (now merged with Dadra & Nagar Haveli); it had high positive growth.

• Lakshadweep (Option 4): A Union Territory; it recorded positive population growth.

question: Who among the following was the chairman of the planning commission under fourth five year plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indira Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Prime Minister was the ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission, so during the Fourth Five Year Plan (1969–1974) the chairperson was Indira Gandhi (इंदिरा गांधी).

• The Fourth Plan emphasised 'growth with stability' and self-reliance.

• The Planning Commission was set up in 1950 to formulate India's Five Year Plans.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

• The Fourth Plan period also saw the nationalisation of banks (1969).

NOTE

• Pitambar Pant (Option 2): An economist and member associated with the Planning Commission, but not its chairman.

• Gulzarilal Nanda (Option 3): A former Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission and twice acting PM, but not the chairman during the Fourth Plan.

• Morarji Desai (Option 4): Later became Prime Minister (1977–79); not the chairman during the Fourth Plan.

question:
Which of the following is a factor responsible for having different types of rural settlements in India?
I. Physical features
II. Social structure
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both physical features and social structure (भौतिक लक्षण और सामाजिक संरचना) are responsible for the different types of rural settlements in India.

• Physical features — relief, altitude, availability of water, soil and climate — decide where and how settlements form (e.g., near water sources).

• Social and cultural factors — caste, community, ethnicity and security — influence the pattern and grouping of houses.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rural settlements are commonly classified as compact/clustered, semi-clustered, hamleted and dispersed.

• Economic factors and security (defence) also shape settlement patterns.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as social structure is also a key factor.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as physical features are equally important.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both stated factors are relevant.

question: Which metal was first used by early human communities in ancient India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Copper.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Copper (तांबा) was the first metal used by early human communities in ancient India.

• The earliest metal age is called the Chalcolithic (Copper-Stone) Age, where copper tools were used alongside stone tools.

• Copper is soft, malleable and could be worked easily, making it the earliest metal to be used.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Later, mixing copper with tin produced bronze, giving the Bronze Age.

• Iron came much later, marking the Iron Age; its use is linked with the Painted Grey Ware culture in India.

NOTE

• Iron (Option 1): Came into use much later than copper, in the Iron Age.

• Bronze (Option 2): An alloy of copper and tin, made only after copper was already in use.

• Gold (Option 3): Known early as an ornamental metal, but not the first metal used for tools/implements.
